tldr: For humanoid loco-manipulation, the authors propose "SP-HLM," a hybrid control framework that combines "just five explicit target poses" (pelvis, both wrists, and both ankles) with a "latent motion representation for whole-body coordination." While drastically easing the burden on the high-level policy, it achieved a 52.75% success rate across eight simulation tasks and demonstrated coordinated whole-body movements on a real humanoid robot.

The upper deployment pipeline shows the motion generation model SP-MGM reconstructing full-body motion from 5-point poses predicted by the VLA, while the motion tracker SP-GMT drives the robot by integrating explicit poses and the latent motion representation. The lower part outlines the training pipeline for each module.
overview:
Humanoid loco-manipulation—performing manipulation tasks while moving—is very challenging due to the large number of full-body degrees of freedom. Existing approaches typically rely on high-level policies (like VLAs) that process camera inputs to either directly predict all joint angles or output abstract motion tokens. However, predicting full-body joints places a heavy burden on high-level policies, whereas motion tokens often struggle with precise end-effector positioning.

To overcome this, the authors came up with the idea of decoupling and combining "spatial task intent" and "natural whole-body coordination" into complementary representations. Specifically, only five task-critical poses (pelvis, both wrists, and both ankles) are explicitly specified, while the coordination of the rest of the body is implicitly filled in via a learned latent motion prior.

To realize this idea, they developed SP-MGM, a fast diffusion model that reconstructs full-body motion in real time from the 5-point sparse targets, and SP-GMT, a whole-body tracker that drives all joints by integrating these 5-point poses with the latent motion variable. Connecting these modules with a VLA, they built the SP-HLM framework and evaluated it in both simulation and the real world.

Experimental results showed that SP-HLM significantly outperformed existing joint-space and token-space baselines in task success rates. Furthermore, on a real Unitree G1 humanoid robot, it smoothly executed demanding daily tasks requiring whole-body coordination, such as shelving while squatting or stepping on a trash can pedal on one leg.
contributions: Proposed a novel humanoid control interface that combines spatial task intent (5-point poses) and whole-body coordination (latent motion representation) in complementary forms.

Developed SP-GMT, a reinforcement learning tracking policy that simultaneously receives explicit sparse targets and an implicit latent motion representation to achieve high-precision whole-body tracking.
Developed SP-MGM, a real-time motion generation model using a two-stage distillation strategy that satisfies 5-point pose constraints while achieving 1.45x faster generation than the baseline.
Built the complete SP-HLM framework with an upstream VLA, demonstrating high task success rates and coordinated whole-body motions across 8 simulation tasks and 4 real-world tasks.

sections.heading: What is the sweet-spot interface between high-level brains and low-level bodies?
sections.summary: In humanoid loco-manipulation, the core design question is how to bridge high-level task policies and low-level whole-body control. This work proposes a complementary interface: explicit sparse poses for 5 task-critical body points (pelvis, both wrists, both ankles) and an implicit latent motion representation for whole-body coordination.
sections.details:
Connecting vision-based high-level task policies with low-level whole-body controllers (WBC) that maintain physical balance has always been a key challenge in humanoid robotics.

Existing interfaces suffer from clear trade-offs:
- Joint-space specification: Although it directly commands all joints, the high-level policy must shoulder not only task intent but also balance and whole-body coordination, making training extremely heavy.
- Task-space specification: Passing only end-effector targets is compact, but sparse targets leave too many degrees of freedom underspecified, making whole-body coordination difficult.
- Token-space specification: Reusing pre-learned motion patterns via discrete tokens is convenient, but it tends to compromise millimeter-level spatial precision at the end effectors.

Here is the key insight. The authors argue that task intent (where to move) should be represented as explicit spatial coordinates, while physical coordination (how to move) should be captured by a learned implicit motion prior.

Specifically, explicit constraints are placed only on the five most critical locations (pelvis, left/right wrists, and left/right ankles), leaving the rest of the coordinated movement to a latent space. This reduces the burden on the high-level policy while achieving both end-effector manipulation precision and natural whole-body dynamics.

sections.heading: How whole-body motion generation and loco-manipulation have evolved
sections.summary: Humanoid research has seen rapid progress in general motion trackers and generative models trained on large motion datasets. However, designing an interface that conveys task intent to whole-body control without burdening the policy or leaving motions underspecified remained largely unexplored.
sections.details:
The related work in this paper spans two main areas.

### II-A General Humanoid Motion Generation and Control
Recent control architectures increasingly insert motion generation models between high-level semantic commands and low-level control, producing dense reference trajectories for lower-level policies to track. In addition, General Motion Trackers (GMT) trained on large-scale motion capture datasets have emerged to provide robust whole-body tracking. However, these focus primarily on imitating given dense trajectories, leaving the design of compact interfaces tailored for loco-manipulation largely unaddressed.

### II-B Interfaces for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
Recent loco-manipulation works using Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models or world models have adopted approaches such as decoupling upper-body manipulation from lower-body locomotion, or directly predicting full-body joint trajectories. The former struggles with flexible, whole-body reaching, while the latter incurs excessive training burdens for the high-level policy. Other attempts using motion tokens sacrifice spatial end-effector precision.

SP-HLM addresses these limitations by uniting explicit sparse targets (5-point poses) with an implicit motion prior (latent variables), filling a critical gap in existing literature.

sections.heading: Inside SP-HLM: Driving the whole body in real time from five poses
sections.summary: SP-HLM consists of three modules: high-level SP-VLA, generative SP-MGM, and tracking SP-GMT. From 5-point poses predicted by the VLA, a distilled fast diffusion model reconstructs full-body motion, and the tracker drives the joints by integrating explicit poses with latent motion.
sections.details:
The full SP-HLM pipeline operates through the collaboration of three main components.

### III-A SP-HLM Overview
At each planning step, SP-VLA predicts 5-point target poses (3D position + 6D rotation for the pelvis, both wrists, and both ankles) and finger joint targets from camera images and language instructions. Next, SP-MGM generates a whole-body trajectory aligned with these five poses, and a pretrained motion encoder compresses this motion into a latent vector $\mathbf{z}_t$. Finally, the low-level SP-GMT tracker takes $\mathbf{z}_t$ and the pelvis-relative 5-point targets to output whole-body joint position commands. Finger targets are passed directly to hand PD controllers.

### III-B SP-GMT: Explicit-Implicit Integrated Whole-Body Tracker
SP-GMT is a reinforcement learning policy that tracks by combining the implicit motion prior with explicit 5-point poses.
- Yaw-Invariant Latent Motion Representation: A Transformer-based motion Variational Autoencoder (VAE) is trained on roughly 190 hours of motion capture data. Poses are aligned to the pelvis yaw and global translations are removed, yielding a compact, local latent representation stripped of redundant information.
- Integrating Explicit and Implicit Inputs: The policy observation $\mathbf{o}^{\pi}_t$ includes the latent vector $\mathbf{z}_t$, pelvis-frame 5-point targets $\mathbf{k}^b_t$, proprioceptive signals (joint angles, angular velocities, pelvis pose, etc.), and the previous action.
- PPO Optimization: In addition to standard whole-body pose and velocity tracking terms, the reward includes a sparse-pose tracking term $r_{\mathrm{sp}}$ that directly evaluates global position and orientation errors of the five points. This keeps limbs precisely on target while maintaining natural whole-body dynamics.

### III-C SP-MGM: Real-Time Motion Generation under Sparse Pose Constraints
To interpolate full-body motion from 5-point poses in real time, the authors compressed an existing diffusion motion generation model (Kimodo) using a novel two-stage distillation strategy.
- Stage I (Offline Supervised Fine-Tuning): A student model with fewer layers and reduced denoising steps is trained on both ground-truth motion data and outputs from the frozen teacher model.
- Stage II (Rollout-Aware Distillation): To prevent error accumulation and distribution shift during inference, the student explores rollout states and receives corrective targets from the teacher. A temporal smoothness regularization loss $L_{\mathrm{temp}}$ is added to suppress high-frequency jitter.

### III-D SP-VLA: Asynchronous Action Prediction
The top-level SP-VLA is based on GR00T N1.7, with only its Flow Matching action head fine-tuned. To hide inference latency, it uses Real-Time Chunking (RTC), keeping the tail of the previous action chunk as a clean prefix and predicting only the suffix. This allows asynchronous execution, generating the next action in the background while the robot executes the current one.

sections.heading: Experimental validation: Leading in tracking, generation speed, and task success
sections.summary: Every module and the overall system were rigorously evaluated. SP-GMT matched SOTA tracking accuracy with minimal training time, while SP-MGM achieved 1.45x faster generation while maintaining precise constraint tracking. SP-HLM demonstrated high success rates across 8 simulation tasks and 4 real-world tasks.
sections.details:
Experiments were designed around three research questions (RQs).

### IV-A Motion Tracking Evaluation (SP-GMT Alone)
Tracking accuracy was tested on unseen motion datasets (Filtered CLOT-500 and BONES-SEED Diverse-500).
- Tracking Accuracy and Training Cost: SP-GMT achieved the lowest global MPJPE (joint position error) and global end-effector (EE) errors across both datasets. Crucially, while SONIC required 21,000 GPU hours and Humanoid-GPT required 15,000 GPU hours, SP-GMT was trained in only 192 GPU hours, demonstrating extraordinary sample efficiency.
- Ablation: Removing the sparse reference sharply worsened global tracking error, while removing the latent reference degraded local joint accuracy. This confirms the necessity of combining explicit 5-point poses with implicit latent representations.

### IV-B Motion Generation Quality and Efficiency (SP-MGM Alone)
SP-MGM was compared against the uncompressed Kimodo baseline (20 denoising steps).
- Accuracy and Speed: SP-MGM reduced both average and 95th-percentile (P95) EE errors compared to Kimodo, while speeding up generation by up to 1.45x (operating at 10 Hz).
- Distillation Ablation: Removing Stage II caused the P95 EE error to jump from 3.212 cm to 12.772 cm. Removing the temporal smoothness loss $L_{\mathrm{temp}}$ degraded the P95 EE jerk by 27.8%, highlighting the importance of two-stage distillation and smoothness regularization.

### IV-C Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation Evaluation (Full System)
Evaluations were conducted on a Unitree G1 robot equipped with a ZED 2i stereo camera.
- Simulation Tasks (8 Tasks): The system was evaluated on eight tasks involving extended whole-body reach, body contact, and mobile picking across 50 trials per task. SP-HLM reached an overall success rate of 52.75%, outperforming token-space and joint-space GR00T baselines. Notably, a variant where the VLA directly predicted latent variables (Direct Latent) plummeted to 23.25%, validating the decoupled design.
- Real-Robot Tasks (4 Tasks): Four daily tasks (object placing, shelving, cabinet opening, and pedal trash can opening) were evaluated over 20 trials each. Placing and shelving achieved over 50% success rates.
- Failure Analysis: The most challenging real-world tasks were cabinet opening in a single-leg squat stance (25% success) and stepping on a narrow trash can pedal on one leg (40% success). These demanded extreme balance, where slight body oscillations caused end-effector misalignment.

sections.heading: Conclusions and what comes next: Integrating dexterous hand manipulation
sections.summary: SP-HLM enables advanced humanoid loco-manipulation by fusing sparse 5-point poses with latent motion representations. Extending this framework to integrate dexterous multi-finger manipulation remains the key future challenge.
sections.details:
This paper presented a sparse-pose-driven interface that treats spatial task intent and whole-body coordination in complementary forms for autonomous humanoid loco-manipulation.

Through three key pillars—SP-VLA predicting 5-point targets and finger commands, SP-MGM reconstructing full-body motion in real time, and SP-GMT performing explicit-implicit integrated tracking—the approach demonstrated strong effectiveness across diverse simulation and real-world tasks.

As a current limitation, the authors note that the framework focuses on whole-body coordination, keeping hand control limited to simple PD control of finger joint positions. A natural next step is extending this sparse-pose-driven architecture to unified, dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered hands.

sections.heading: Appendix: Implementation details and training hyperparameters
sections.summary: This section summarizes key implementation details for reproducibility, including reward design for SP-GMT, distillation settings for SP-MGM, and RTC configurations for SP-VLA.
sections.details:
The paper's appendix specifies training parameters for each module:

- SP-GMT Reward Design: Built on top of BeyondMimic's reward formulation, it adds global position and orientation tracking rewards for the four limb end effectors (wrists and ankles), along with penalties to suppress unnecessary foot movements.
- SP-MGM Training Details: Compressed in layer depth and diffusion steps from the Kimodo baseline. Stage I performs offline distillation against the teacher model and ground-truth motion data, while Stage II applies relabeling on rollout states along with temporal smoothness regularization.
- SP-VLA Inference Settings: Fine-tuned from GR00T N1.7 for 160k steps. It outputs a 40-step action chunk (59 dimensions: 14 for hand joints, 9 for pelvis pose, and 9 for each of the four limb endpoints). RTC latency is randomized between 0 and 8 steps. During deployment, the first 34 steps are executed while the remaining 6 steps serve as a prefix for the next prediction in a rolling-horizon fashion. With TensorRT optimization, SP-VLA runs at 25 Hz and SP-MGM runs at 10 Hz in real time.

takeaways: Representing task targets (spatial poses of limbs and pelvis) and motion style (whole-body coordination) through a hybrid of explicit and implicit representations works far better than forcing them into a single representation.

Applying two-stage distillation (rollout-aware re-labeling and temporal smoothness regularization) to a diffusion-based motion generator enables real-time 10 Hz generation without losing constraint accuracy.
Using a yaw-invariant latent motion representation allows training a whole-body tracker to SOTA-level accuracy in just 192 GPU hours, drastically cutting computational costs.
In VLA action-chunk prediction, an asynchronous RTC mechanism that reuses the tail of the previous action as a prefix is essential for smooth, continuous real-world execution.
limitations: Hand control is limited to joint-position PD control, leaving contact-rich, dexterous manipulation (such as in-hand reorientation) unsupported.
In postures requiring extreme balance, such as single-leg squats or single-leg pedal pressing, slight body oscillations cause end-effector tracking deviations, lowering real-world success rates.
